## Edge-striped ray propagation variant (separate from panel counting)
For full-size grids with edge bars and sparse markers rather than panel partitions, demos may show edge-originating bands and horizontal marker rays. Treat this as a distinct task family, not the panel-counting rule: infer output color/direction and exact boundaries from demos, preserve unrelated cells, and avoid filling all edge-adjacent background automatically. In examples, 2 markers became 4 at ray sources and intermediate cells took the appropriate propagated color while an opposite-boundary edge cell remained unchanged. The edge-ray behavior needs demo-specific verification.

## Confirmed task-8e04f0ad variant: replicate the occupied panel pattern across a separator grid
Full uniform horizontal and vertical separators partition the grid into equal-sized rectangular panels. One panel contains a structured pattern (including field/background cells), while the other panels are empty/uniform. Copy the entire pattern panel cell-for-cell into every panel, preserving every separator line. The source panel need not be the lowest band or even the same panel location across instances; identify it from the unique structured content in the current grid. This includes copying the pattern across both axes, not merely repeating one horizontal band.

Verified demo: 15x11 input with full separator column 5 and row 7 forms a 2x2 array of 7x5 panels. The structured pattern is in the upper-right panel (rows 0–6, cols 6–10); output repeats that exact panel into upper-left, lower-left, and lower-right. Separator row/column remain unchanged. Accepted test: 23x5 input with full separator rows 7 and 15 and separator column 2 forms a 3x2 array of 7x2 panels. The structured pattern is in the middle-right panel (rows 8–14, cols 3–4); its entire 7x2 content is repeated in all six panels, preserving both horizontal separator rows and the vertical separator column. Crucially, copy all cells, including field-valued cells, rather than only sparse markers. Validate panel dimensions and replicate the source panel in top-to-bottom/left-to-right alignment.

Earlier evidence for this task ID had been summarized as copying a bottom-band pattern vertically; the present demo/test show the broader two-dimensional panel replication variant. Do not assume source-panel location or only vertical repetition from task ID alone.

# Striped panel pair-count decoding

Use when full-length uniform separator rows and columns divide a grid into rectangular panels. Panels contain a field/background color plus sparse cells of a distinct marker color, and expected output is a much smaller grid.

1. Locate complete uniform separator lines; treat them as dividers, not output.
2. Partition the area between dividers into panels. Output dimensions equal panel rows by panel columns.
3. Count sparse marker-color cells in each panel. In the demonstrated variant, output `1` when a panel has **exactly two** markers; otherwise output the panel's field/background color. Confirm colors and count rule from demos before applying.
5. Preserve panel order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). Do not count divider cells.
6. Validate every panel against the demos, especially zero-, one-, and two-marker panels. Output the panel matrix, not the original grid size. Infer colors per instance, never hard-code example colors.

## Verified 2x2-panel variant
A confirmed instance used background 3, sparse marker 2, full separator rows and columns of 9, and 2x2 panels. Each panel became 1 iff it contained exactly two marker cells; a panel with one marker became background 3. A larger 5x4-panel demo confirmed the same exact-two rule, including panels with one or two markers. Thus the rule applies to panel marker counts, not panel dimensions or marker arrangement; count only cells inside each panel.

Demonstrations confirmed the same rule with different colors: a panel maps to 1 iff it contains exactly two sparse markers; otherwise it maps to its field color. Infer colors per instance, never hard-code example colors.

## Confirmed task-2442e88d recurrence: exact-two sparse marker panels
Full uniform separator rows and columns partition the grid into panels; emit one output cell per panel in top-to-bottom, left-to-right order. Across three demonstrations/test, a panel maps to output 1 iff it contains exactly two sparse marker cells; otherwise it maps to that instance's field/background color. Count only panel cells, excluding separators; panel dimensions and palette can vary.

Detailed recurrence evidence: Demo 1 input 19x14 had separator rows 4, 9, 14 and columns 4, 9 (0-indexed), making a 4x3 array of 4x4 panels. Background 9, marker 6, separator 2. The output was [[1,9,9],[9,9,9],[1,9,1],[9,9,1]]. Demo 2 input 17x5 had separator rows 5,11 and column 2, making a 3x2 panel array of 5x2 panels. Background 6, marker 7, separator 9. Output [[1,1],[1,6],[1,1]] confirms exactly-two rather than any-marker counting (the one-marker panel outputs 6).

Accepted test input 14x7 had separators rows 4,9 and column 3, yielding 3x2 panels with sizes 4x3/4x3 on first two panel rows and 3x3/3x3 on the last. Background 4, marker 7, separator 2. Panel marker counts were [[2,2],[2,2],[2,1]], and the correct output was [[1,1],[1,1],[1,4]]. Exclude all separator cells from counts. This recurrence independently confirms the rule with differing panel sizes, separators, and palette.

Further accepted task-2442e88d test recurrence: input 14x15 used full separator rows 4 and 9, and separator columns 3, 7, and 11, producing 3x4 panels. Background 4, sparse marker 8. The panel counts were [[2,2,2,2],[2,1,2,2],[2,2,1,2]], so the accepted output was [[1,1,1,1],[1,4,1,1],[1,1,4,1]]. This confirms the exact-two rule for four panel columns and panel heights 4, 4, and 4/3; a panel with exactly one marker maps to background 4.

A further accepted task-2442e88d instance had a 19x11 input with full separator rows 3, 7, 11, 15 and full separator columns 2, 5, 8, forming a 5x4 array of 3x2 panels. Background was 5 and sparse marker 8. The output was [[5,1,5,1],[1,1,1,5],[1,5,5,5],[5,1,5,5],[5,1,1,1]], confirming precisely two markers -> 1 and every other panel -> background, including panels with one marker and panels with more than two.

Another accepted instance had a 19x9 input with full separator rows 4, 9, 14 and separator column 4, forming 4x2 panels of 4x4 cells. Background was 4, sparse marker 7; exact-two marker counts by panel were [[2,2],[1,2],[2,1],[1,1]], and output was [[1,1],[4,1],[1,1],[4,4]]. The first test guess was incorrect because it used the wrong non-exact-two output color (5); the demo established that other panels retain the field/background color, not a fixed color.
